sentences.zh: 诺亚·沙尼是《造假的艺术：艺术造假大师的心理、动机与手法》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Coming up, I explore why we find art forgers so compelling and why we like studies that show
sentences.zh: 接下来，我将探讨为什么我们觉得艺术造假者如此引人入胜，以及为什么我们喜欢那些表明

sentences.en: that wine connoisseurs don't know what they're talking about.
sentences.zh: 葡萄酒鉴赏家其实根本不懂他们在说什么的研究。

sentences.en: Stanford professor Baba Shiv
sentences.zh: 斯坦福大学教授巴巴·希夫

sentences.en: tells us about an interesting experiment.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲述了一个有趣的实验。

sentences.en: People always swear that when they taste a higher-priced wine, the wine actually tastes better.
sentences.zh: 人们总是发誓说，当他们品尝价格更高的葡萄酒时，酒的味道确实更好。

sentences.en: They derive more pleasure from the higher-priced wine.
sentences.zh: 他们从价格更高的葡萄酒中获得了更多的愉悦感。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I've asked myself why I find the story of Eric Hebburn so compelling.
sentences.zh: 我曾问过自己，为什么我发现埃里克·赫本的故事如此引人入胜。

sentences.en: He was a criminal, but I think of him as a Robin Hood-type criminal.
sentences.zh: 他是个罪犯，但我认为他属于罗宾汉式的罪犯。

sentences.en: Part of it is because, as Noah Charney said, art crime doesn't disturb us.
sentences.zh: 部分原因正如诺亚·沙尼所说，艺术犯罪不会打扰我们。

sentences.en: In fact, as Dennis Leary's detective character in the 1999 movie The Thomas Crown Affair says,
sentences.zh: 事实上，正如1999年电影《偷天陷阱》中丹尼斯·利瑞饰演的侦探角色所说，

sentences.en: the stakes for art crime are pretty low, unless you're a member of the 1%.
sentences.zh: 艺术犯罪的代价相当低，除非你是那百分之一的富豪。

sentences.en: The week before I met you, I nailed two crooked real estate agents and a guy who was beating his kids to death.
sentences.zh: 就在我见到你前一个星期，我刚抓了两个贪腐的房地产经纪人和一个把自己的孩子往死里打的家伙。

sentences.en: So if some Houdini wants to snatch a couple swirls of paint, that are really only important to some very silly, rich people.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有什么胡迪尼想偷走几抹颜料，那些东西其实只对某些非常愚蠢的富人重要。

sentences.en: I don't really give up.
sentences.zh: 我才不在乎呢。

sentences.en: But there's another reason Hebburn is a compelling figure.
sentences.zh: 但赫本成为一个迷人人物还有另一个原因。

sentences.en: Most of us don't understand the world of art, and we have the vague suspicion that people who claim to know what they're talking about are faking it.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人并不了解艺术世界，我们隐约怀疑那些声称自己懂行的人其实是在装懂。

sentences.en: So Hebburn wasn't just making a fast buck.
sentences.zh: 所以赫本不只是在捞快钱。

sentences.en: He was waging a populist war.
sentences.zh: 他在发动一场平民主义的战争。

sentences.en: I sometimes feel this way about people who talk about a bottle of wine that has
sentences.zh: 有时我对那些谈论一瓶带有

sentences.en: a hint of briny oyster shell riding the lacy mousse.
sentences.zh: 蕾丝泡沫般咸鲜生蚝壳气息的葡萄酒的人也有这种感觉。

sentences.en: That's an actual quote from a recent wine review.
sentences.zh: 这是最近一篇葡萄酒评论中的原话。

sentences.en: Psychological studies show that when you pour cheap wine from an expensive bottle,
sentences.zh: 心理学研究表明，当你把廉价酒倒入昂贵的酒瓶时，

sentences.en: wine aficionados say,
sentences.zh: 葡萄酒爱好者会说，

sentences.en: ah, that wine has flavors of lightly toasted brioche, spun honey, and glazed apricot.
sentences.zh: 啊，这酒有轻度烤面包、流质蜂蜜和糖渍杏子的风味。

sentences.en: Baba Shiv is a marketing professor at Stanford.
sentences.zh: 巴巴·希夫是斯坦福大学的市场营销学教授。

sentences.en: He recently invited wine connoisseurs to a blind taste teSt.
sentences.zh: 他最近邀请了葡萄酒鉴赏家参加一项盲品测试。

sentences.en: They refused to show up.
sentences.zh: 他们拒绝出席。

sentences.en: Why did they refuse to come?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么拒绝来呢？

sentences.en: You have someone who is in a vineyard and supposed to be an expert in tasting wine,
sentences.zh: 如果你有一个身处葡萄园本应是品酒专家的人，

sentences.en: and now if I invite them over here, and we find out that they're no different than the novices,
sentences.zh: 而现在如果我把他们请到这里来，结果发现他们和新手没什么两样，

sentences.en: then there goes the reputation, in a way.
sentences.zh: 那么，从某种意义上说，名声就毁了。

sentences.en: Okay, so that totally confirms my view that these connoisseurs weren't really experts.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这完全证实了我的看法，即这些鉴赏家并不是真正的专家。

sentences.en: But here's where the science gets in the way of a nice theory.
sentences.zh: 但科学在这里却与一个美好的理论产生了冲突。

sentences.en: Something happened in Baba Shiv's wine experiment that shook my populist sensibilities.
sentences.zh: 巴巴·希夫的葡萄酒实验中发生了一件事，动摇了我的平民主义情结。

sentences.en: The researchers put volunteers in a brain scanner, gave them different wines.
sentences.zh: 研究人员让志愿者进入脑部扫描仪，给他们喝不同的葡萄酒。

sentences.en: These were occasional wine drinkers, not experts.
sentences.zh: 这些都是偶尔喝红酒的人，而不是专家。

sentences.en: Some wines from $5 bottles were said to be from a $45 bottle.
sentences.zh: 其中一些售价5美元的酒被告知是45美元的酒。

sentences.en: Other wines from a $90 bottle were said to be from a $10 bottle.
sentences.zh: 另一些售价90美元的酒则被告知是10美元的酒。

sentences.en: The volunteers said that wine from the more expensive bottles tasted better compared to the same wine poured from a supposedly cheap bottle.
sentences.zh: 志愿者们表示，与从据称廉价的酒瓶中倒出的同一种酒相比，从更贵酒瓶中倒出的酒味道更好。

sentences.en: All right, score one for the populace.
sentences.zh: 好吧，平民主义得一分。

sentences.en: The wine drinkers were fooled.
sentences.zh: 这些品酒者被骗了。

sentences.en: But here's where it gets complicated.
sentences.zh: 但复杂的地方来了。

sentences.en: The researchers examined the brain scans of the volunteers.
sentences.zh: 研究人员检查了志愿者的脑部扫描结果。

sentences.en: So what we found, essentially, is that the area of the brain that codes for pleasure, which is the ventromedial prefrontal cortex,
sentences.zh: 所以我们基本上发现，大脑中编码愉悦感的区域，也就是腹内侧前额叶皮层，

sentences.en: this is the area of the brain that codes for pleasure in real time and has been documented in other studies.
sentences.zh: 这是大脑中实时编码愉悦感并在其他研究中得到记录的区域。

sentences.en: And what we found, essentially, was that this area of the brain that codes for pleasure in real time shows greater activation
sentences.zh: 我们基本上发现，大脑中这个实时编码愉悦感的区域表现出更强的激活度，

sentences.en: when the brain thinks it is tasting a higher-priced wine than when the brain thinks it is tasting a lower-priced wine.
sentences.zh: 当大脑认为自己品尝的是高价酒时，比大脑认为自己品尝的是低价酒时要强。

sentences.en: The volunteers, in other words, weren't merely saying the wine from the expensive bottle tasted better
sentences.zh: 换句话说，志愿者们不仅仅是因为觉得那是他们应该说的话，

sentences.en: because they thought that's what they were supposed to say.
sentences.zh: 才说昂贵瓶子里的酒更好喝的。

sentences.en: The volunteers actually did experience the wine differently.
sentences.zh: 志愿者们对酒的实际体验确实不同。

sentences.en: It tasted better.
sentences.zh: 它确实更好喝了。

sentences.en: If you have expectations about how much pleasure you're going to derive from, let us say, wine,
sentences.zh: 如果你对你将从（比方说）葡萄酒中获得多少愉悦感有所期待，

sentences.en: your expectations actually turn into reality.
sentences.zh: 你的期待确实会变成现实。

sentences.en: The difference between a $200 bottle of wine and a bottle that costs $8.99 is only partly about the wine.
sentences.zh: 一瓶200美元的葡萄酒和一瓶8.99美元的葡萄酒之间的差距，只有一部分与酒本身有关。

sentences.en: If paying more for a bottle of wine makes you want to save it for a special occasion,
sentences.zh: 如果为一瓶酒支付更多费用让你想要把它留到特殊场合，

sentences.en: share it with good friends over a meal, savor it, then yes, that bottle of wine will taste better.
sentences.zh: 在用餐时与好朋友分享，细细品味，那么是的，那瓶酒就会更好喝。

sentences.en: It's exactly the same with art.
sentences.zh: 艺术完全也是如此。

sentences.en: Forgers show us that experts can be fooled, but they also miss something important.
sentences.zh: 造假者向我们展示了专家是可以被欺骗的，但他们也忽略了一些重要的事情。

sentences.en: The value of a painting is only partly about the painting itself.
sentences.zh: 一幅画的价值只有一部分与画作本身有关。

sentences.en: When you look at a masterpiece, you are looking at paint on canvas.
sentences.zh: 当你看着一幅杰作时，你看到的是画布上的颜料。

sentences.en: But that isn't all you're doing.
sentences.zh: 但你所做的远不止于此。

sentences.en: You're thinking about Monet's hand holding the paintbrush.
sentences.zh: 你在脑海中想着莫奈握着画笔的手。

sentences.en: You're thinking about history, the passage of time.
sentences.zh: 你在想着历史，时间的流逝。

sentences.en: The meaning of the painting isn't just what's on the canvas.
sentences.zh: 画作的意义不仅仅在于画布上的内容。

sentences.en: It's what you bring to it.
sentences.zh: 还在于你为它赋予了什么。

sentences.en: When Hebron's preparatory drawings were revealed to be forgeries,
sentences.zh: 当赫本的预备草图被揭露是赝品时，

sentences.en: the drawings didn't change.
sentences.zh: 草图本身并没有变。

sentences.en: But something did change in our mind.
sentences.zh: 但我们心中的某些东西确实变了。

sentences.en: Instead of making us think about history and time,
sentences.zh: 这些草图不再让我们联想到历史和时间，

sentences.en: the drawings were now merely clever.
sentences.zh: 而是仅仅显得很聪明。

sentences.en: They stopped being masterpieces.
sentences.zh: 它们不再是杰作了。
